output_list.reason: The mintToken function has an integer overflow vulnerability. The initial supply is set in the constructor, minted to the owner, and can be exploited to overflow the balanceOf mapping, causing a denial of service to any potential buyers.

The transfer function has an integer overflow vulnerability. The _transfer function has a require statement that checks if the balanceOf[_from] is greater than or equal to _value, and balanceOf[_to] + _value is greater than balanceOf[_to]. However, due to integer overflow, if balanceOf[_from] is at the maximum value of a uint256, and _value is non-zero, the requirement will be bypassed, allowing a transfer from [_from] to [_to] of a value greater than balanceOf[_from].

The transferFrom function has an integer overflow vulnerability. The _transfer function has a require statement that checks if balanceOf[_to] + _value is greater than balanceOf[_to]. However, due to integer overflow, if balanceOf[_to] is at the maximum value of a uint256, and _value is non-zero, the requirement will be bypassed, allowing a transfer from [_from] to [_to] of a value greater than balanceOf[_from].

The approve function has an integer overflow vulnerability. The approve function increases the allowance mapping, which can be exploited to overflow the allowance mapping, causing a denial of service to any spender.

The burnFrom function has an integer overflow vulnerability. The _transfer function has a require statement that checks if balanceOf[_from] is greater than or equal to _value, and allowance[_from][msg.sender] is greater than or equal to _value. However, due to integer overflow, if balanceOf[_from] is at the maximum value of a uint256, and _value is non-zero, the requirement will be bypassed, allowing a burnFrom from [_from] of a value greater than allowance[_from][msg.sender].
